chunk_map.heading: How we work in this room

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: an unresolved referent strands a reader mid-deck; absent here. Chunk 0's "M1" is the arc-earned module-name carve-out. Chunk 2's "this module"/"here" resolve to chunk 0. Chunk 5 "prior modules" is a generic class, not a specific unnamed artefact. Chunk 7 defines "the loop" and "context" in the same bullet before reuse. Chunk 8's "./CLAUDE.local.md" callback resolves to chunk 3 where it was first named. Chunk 9's "it" (Module 2) resolves via its own header.

Harm: a positional callback strands a reader who enters through a different deck path; absent here. Chunk 2's prework pointer is named, not located (the prior "at the top of this workbook" locator is confirmed cut per the maintainer block and `check-slide-deixis.js` returns clean for this file). Chunk 9 names every pre-read by title/author. No file is referenced by position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a dead "the thing you did" reference sends a student hunting for a removed beat; no such backward-beat construction appears in this module opener's own body (chunk 6's link text "The machine you just met" is a title, not a claim asserted in this file's prose).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: an outcome narrated before its guess breaks a live-demo beat; no guess-before-reveal construction appears anywhere in this module-overview body.
Harm: a wait-state-only chunk projects as an empty slide; absent here. Every chunk (0-9) carries a self-contained claim, instruction, or list.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts misleads a skimming reader; absent across chunks 1-9. "Freedom to choose" accurately heads the four choice-bullets, "Start here" accurately heads the trick-share question plus the module's link list, "Next" accurately heads the Module 2 bridge.

Harm: cadence tics substitute rhythm for content and can leak self-praise; absent across chunks 0-9. Chunk 5's "Not too fast, not too slow" is a single comma-joined two-part bound, not the banned period-separated "Not X. Not Y. Z." triple. No anaphora triple, self-grading superlative, number-with-retraction, abstraction-noun stack, or empty verb triplet found elsewhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: maintainer-register vocabulary projected to students speaks the curriculum's private dialect rather than the room's; absent across chunks 0-9. "working memory", "trainer", "exercises", "modules" are ordinary student-facing training terms; repo-internal terms (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections-as-proper-noun) appear only below the maintainer cut, out of scope for this rule.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: sentence-scale or ubiquitous bold makes emphasis stop signalling usable handles; absent here. Chunk 3's five verb leads (Run/Distinguish/Fix/Close/Compound), chunk 4's three checklist-item names (All learners/Exercises/Share and discuss), chunk 6's single "The question (to you):" handle, and chunk 9's Read/Watch labels are all sub-5-word handles per the rule's own "checklist item names" category, not bolded lead sentences. No chunk bolds a full sentence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: module prose visible only in long-read disappears from the classroom's default Slides view; absent. `node --test scripts/slides.test.js` ran clean (23/23 pass), including the module-level-prose-interleaved and anchor-resolution guards that this file's top-level `## ` sections depend on.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: hand-numbered content drifts on reorder; no Phase/Step header or in-file Phase/Step reference appears in this module opener. `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js` returned OK across all 60 scanned files. "Module 2" is a stable cross-module identifier, not a hand-numbered slide position.
